decisions.evidence: Overall, the high ionizable-site count, high TPSA, multiple basic sites, and sulfonamide burden outweigh the favorable neutral fraction and moderate QED, so the molecule is more consistent with poor intestinal absorption and is better classified as cannot be absorbed.
Because the unfavorable ionization and polar-functional-group pattern is persistent across all six comparisons, the overall evidence still supports option (A): cannot be absorbed.
